film-crew.name: Film Crew
film-crew.tagline: A full crew — researcher, writer, designer, sound, subtitler and publisher — that turns a topic into a finished film.
film-crew.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
highlights: One command: /director --paper --topic “…” --shorts 3 --parts 2 --publish
Sixteen stages, fifteen crew skills — discovered from the filesystem, never hard-coded
An animation director budgets motion like a TV anime budgets drawings, and measures the result
Characters that perform: a jointed rig, squash and stretch, comic holds — on twos, over backgrounds on ones
Every visual style is a skill of its own; installing one adds a look and changes no code
Research, sound, captions and rights clearance are separate roles with their own gates
Publishing needs approval bound to the exact bytes; re-render and it lapses

skillDescriptions.director: Runs the whole production. Parses the brief, picks or ranks the style, fans the work out into episodes and Shorts, and drives the crew stage by stage — refusing to call anything done without an artifact behind it, and refusing to publish without approval bound to the exact file.
skillDescriptions.screenwriter: Turns the researcher's ledger into narration that is accurate to the second and to the fact: every line bound to a claim, contested numbers left hedged, sized to the runtime budget before the first sentence is written, and linted before it counts as a deliverable.
skillDescriptions.story-editor: Engineers a script so people keep watching — the opening three seconds, the open loops that hold the middle, and an ending that earns a rewatch. Hook taxonomy, re-hook vocabulary, cut-rhythm and caption specs, and the rules for writing narration a neural TTS engine can actually perform. Separates what YouTube actually documents from creator method and folklore, and lints every promise against its payoff.
skillDescriptions.storyboard-artist: Turns a finished script into a beat plan: what appears on screen, on which spoken word, and which moments are worth cutting as Shorts. Deliberately style-neutral, so the same plan can be shot in any style — with a validator that checks pacing, that on-screen keywords are actually spoken, and that every open loop is paid.
skillDescriptions.animation-director: Decides how much motion every beat gets, the way a TV anime ships an episode on 3,000 drawings instead of 12,000 — most shots held nearly still so one or two can have everything. Allocates a style-neutral motion budget across five tiers, then measures the finished render to prove the loud beats really are louder than the quiet ones.
skillDescriptions.production-designer: Owns the look. Holds the style registry, ranks styles against a topic, compiles a beat plan into the chosen style's storyboard and renders it. A style is just a folder, so new looks drop in without code changes — and a style that cannot draw what a beat asks for says so rather than substituting something close.
skillDescriptions.voice-booth: Generates natural-sounding voiceovers and narrations using edge-tts. Creates high-quality neural audio files from text, with pacing and pauses tailored for video production, and measures every clip so the storyboard can be timed against it.
skillDescriptions.head-of-marketing: Packages a finished video for YouTube: a searchable bilingual title, description, chapters and tags, a thumbnail built to survive a 168px search result, a subscribe-and-bell outro, and limit linting against every field YouTube will reject. It writes the package; it never uploads it.
skillDescriptions.publisher: Uploads to YouTube and nothing else. Publishing is the one irreversible step in the plugin, so every upload, edit, thumbnail and privacy change is gated on an approval bound to the sha256 of the exact bytes a human saw — re-render the file and the approval lapses rather than carrying over.
skillDescriptions.tn-assembly: Turns one long assembly or parliament webcast into a set of publishable videos. Detects highlights and heated exchanges from the audio, derives how many episodes the session actually justifies, cuts every segment on natural speech boundaries at full resolution, and builds branded long-form episodes plus vertical Shorts that route viewers back.
skillDescriptions.researcher: Establishes what is true before anyone writes a sentence. Two independent sources per claim, verbatim quotes stored, contradictions recorded rather than resolved, and gaps written down so nothing gets asserted just because it sounded right.
skillDescriptions.sound-designer: Decides what the film sounds like underneath the voice: mood, music bed, ducking keyed to the narration envelope, and one final mix whose loudness is measured and reported rather than assumed.
skillDescriptions.subtitler: Writes the caption file the platform actually indexes — timed from the rendered storyboard, broken at clauses for reading speed, and spelling the proper nouns the way the ledger spells them instead of the way a recogniser guesses them.
skillDescriptions.rights-manager: The last gate before an upload that cannot be taken back: every asset's licence and attribution on record, and every figure and superlative in the title checked back against the ledger. Refuses by default; exceptions must be reasoned and recorded.
skillDescriptions.style-paper: A documentary researcher's pinboard — aged paper, torn photographs, typewriter labels and one red pen. Suits history, disaster, investigation and science.
skillDescriptions.style-news: A rolling news bulletin — full-bleed footage under a stacked kicker and headline, channel bug and location chip. Suits journalism, business and breaking events.
skillDescriptions.render-farm: A second picture pipeline, orthogonal to every style: renders a film through Remotion — React and SVG in a headless browser — instead of compositing it in PIL. Measured 5.5× faster on the same board, with a scrubbable timeline and hot reload. Either trace an existing style so no artwork is redrawn, or author a film natively in React.
skillDescriptions.style-2d-animation: Flat-vector characters that actually perform — a jointed rig with weight, squash and stretch, comic holds and real cuts. Characters animate on twos while backgrounds and camera stay on ones, the way the reference films do. Suits comedy, chases and character-led stories.

skillDescriptions.app-store-listing: Guide for App Store Connect metadata and ASO — what Apple indexes, keyword budgeting, why competitor names are a 2.3.7 rejection, categories, pricing and featuring nominations.
skillDescriptions.app-store-release: Guide for App Store release management, phased releases, App Review guidelines, version bumps, fastlane, and TestFlight distribution.
skillDescriptions.app-store-submission: Guide for App Store submission — privacy questionnaires, export compliance, age ratings, demo accounts, per-platform review notes, and the 2.1 / 2.1(b) rejection playbooks.
skillDescriptions.architecture: Guide for iOS app architecture, Target layout, WidgetKit extensions, App Groups, Xcode project structure, shared code, and data flow.
skillDescriptions.build-and-run: Guide for xcodebuild, CLI simulator launching, scheme configurations, UDID targeting, provisioning profiles, code signing, and CLI testing.
skillDescriptions.clock-faces: Guide for SwiftUI continuous animation, clock widgets, dense timelines, TimelineProvider, rotating hands, CADisplayLink, and rendering ticks.
skillDescriptions.conventions: Guide for iOS Swift coding conventions, SwiftUI style, async/await usage, unowned/weak self, explicit types, trailing closures, and project rules.
skillDescriptions.feedback: Guide for implementing an in-app feedback and bug reporting loop without authenticated SDKs. Triggers on keywords like feedback, report an issue, contact us, Firebase REST, unauthenticated Firestore, URLSession.
skillDescriptions.in-app-purchases: Guide for In-App Purchases (Apple IAP / StoreKit 2) and payment integration. Triggers on keywords like IAP, StoreKit, subscription, paywall, non-consumable, revenue, restore purchases.
skillDescriptions.ios-agent-guide: Master index for iOS development rules, invariants, App Groups, WidgetKit limits, App Store constraints, and agent troubleshooting playbook.
skillDescriptions.macos-app: Shipping a Mac target: window lifecycle, the Window menu, Dock reopen, and the Guideline 4 rejection for a closed window that cannot be reopened.
skillDescriptions.qa-and-reviews: Guide for QA testing, app reviews, and multi-agent code audits. Triggers on keywords like QA, review, audit, functional test, bug hunt, and multi-agent.
skillDescriptions.realtime-widgets: Guide for real-time widgets, live activities, Dynamic Island, push to wake, background timeline refreshes, and high-frequency WidgetKit updates.
skillDescriptions.simulator-automation: Guide for xcrun simctl, simulator automation, UI testing, automated screenshot capture, device pairing, and headless iOS testing.
skillDescriptions.store-screenshots: Guide for generating App Store screenshots — script-driven frames, squircle device bezels, composing for the search thumbnail, and the marketing-honesty rules.
skillDescriptions.telemetry: Guide for Firebase Analytics (GA4), custom events, user properties, session tracking, crashlytics, and privacy-preserving telemetry without PII.
skillDescriptions.theming: Guide for SwiftUI theming, dark mode, color schemes, dynamic colors, asset catalogs, typography, branding, and style-aware widget designs.
skillDescriptions.transparency: Guide for iOS transparent widgets, background baking, wallpaper cropping, host transparency hacks, coordinate math, and blending UI components.
skillDescriptions.weatherkit: Guide for Apple WeatherKit integration, App Services provisioning, WeatherService APIs, CoreLocation, attribution requirements, and data caching.

azure.name: Azure — Skill as Compute
azure.tagline: Rents an Azure VM for the heavy part of a job, then destroys it.
azure.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
highlights: One call: offload — create, upload, run, download, destroy
Sizes the machine to a monthly budget (default ₹10,000, shown in USD)

skillDescriptions.compute: The way any other skill borrows compute. Hands a compute-intense task to a temporary Azure VM sized to fit your budget, runs it there, brings the results back, and deletes the whole resource group.
